=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:2449-2454 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: The existing `unblock_fixup_origin` check in `unblock_main` calls `unblock_escalate_fixup` and returns 0 before control reaches the new #9946 no-wait "nothing to implement" close guard (lines 2457-2475). So that guard can never run for an issue with a fix-up origin, including a judge-filed fix-up issue.
  WHY: Both reviewers rated it MAJOR, so the two agree. The escalation happens only once, and later runs log `outcome=skip reason=fixup_escalated` (lines 1775-1782) and still return 0, so a fix-up issue whose work is already on the planning ref stays open with `ai:blocked` forever and needs a manual close. That is the failure #9946 set out to fix. Note: anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 checked this claim and rejected it in its review notes (it calls this the existing Q56 exit, says the issue's Non-goals rule out changing the fix-up path, and says keeping the escalation is the lower-risk behaviour).
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: “Add a call to the same function on the no-pending-wait path for standalone ai:blocked issues, before the judge would resume or escalate.”
  expected_change_site: scripts/unblock_judge.sh, unblock_main, before the blocked-fix-up escalation return.
  confidence=4
  flagged_by: [openai_gpt-6-luna]
  EVIDENCE: At lines 2449-2453, when unblock_fixup_origin returns an origin, the judge calls unblock_escalate_fixup and returns. The new no-wait close call comes later, at lines 2467-2474, so a qualifying blocked fix-up with no pending wait is escalated without reaching the close helper. The existing test at tests/test_unblock_judge.py:3704-3714 confirms that a pipeline-authored fix-up marker on an ai:blocked issue takes this early-return path.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_3-flash ===
- scripts/unblock_judge.sh:unblock_main, lines 2449-2454 (the Q56 blocked-fixup deterministic exit) vs the #9946 guard at lines 2457-2475 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The no-wait "nothing to implement" close cannot be reached for a judge-filed fix-up issue. `unblock_fixup_origin` (line 1761) matches any issue whose body starts with a trusted `<!-- ai:unblock-fixup:v1 item=N round=R -->` marker. On a match, lines 2451-2453 call `unblock_escalate_fixup` and `return 0` unconditionally, so control never reaches the #9946 guard at line 2467. The escalation happens only once (lines 1775-1782 log `outcome=skip reason=fixup_escalated`), so after the first escalation the issue is skipped permanently.
  WHY: A fix-up issue whose work turned out to be already on the planning ref is escalated to a human once and then stays open with `ai:blocked` forever, needing a manual close. This is the #9215-class failure that #9946 set out to fix. The linked issue does not authorize an escalation carve-out, even though the agents.d fragment documents the current ordering.
=== END FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_3-flash ===
